summary: A symposium held on September 18, 2023 brought together technology education experts to discuss the future of e-learning platforms and distance education. Speakers forecast that adaptive learning, VR/AR, big data analytics, ubiquitous learning, social collaboration tools, lifelong learning, AI, and gamification will reshape how people learn over the next decade. The note concludes that these technologies promise an unprecedented revolution in learning, teaching and skills development.
one_line: Experts at a September 2023 symposium forecast how adaptive learning, VR/AR, big data, AI, and gamification will transform e-learning and distance education.
key_facts: The symposium on e-learning platforms and distance education took place on September 18, 2023.
Dr. Emily Zhao, a professor at Thornhill University and keynote speaker, forecast that in the next decade e-learning platforms will become "more intuitive, personalized, and learner-centric."

Adaptive learning curates content to each student's needs and pace, using algorithms to analyze performance; challenging content is revisited in various formats until mastery while areas of strength are accelerated.
Leo Gibson, CEO of NextGen EduTech, introduced his company's latest innovation and gave the example of studying marine biology by diving into the Great Barrier Reef via a VR headset.
VR and AR are anticipated to become commonplace in e-learning platforms by the end of this decade, offering simulations of real-world environments.
Sandra Clarke, a data strategist at EduData Solutions, said big data analytics will let institutions tailor learning, predict student outcomes, and identify at-risk students before they fall behind.
Amir Patel, an edtech investor, described 'ubiquitous learning' as learning no longer confined to classrooms or specific times, available anytime, anywhere, on any device.

Dr. Jane Milton, a researcher in educational technology, predicted collaborative tools that mimic social media interaction, such as forums, shared workspaces and peer reviews, will play a massive role in e-learning.
Jorge Alvarez, a human resources executive at a leading tech company, argued e-learning platforms are the ideal medium for continuous professional development.
Customizable professional modules are expected to offer certifications and micro-credentials that professionals accumulate over their careers.
Dr. Fiona Cartwright, a computer scientist specializing in AI, proposed that AI might design curriculum in real time and generate learning resources as needed.
AI could serve as a personal tutor, offer proactive interventions when students struggle, and grade assignments, freeing educators to focus on more complex aspects of teaching.
Gamification uses points, levels, and badges to boost engagement and is expected to increase retention rates in future e-learning platforms.
